claims.text: Fortinbras was the son of Isumbras IV. He married Lalia Clayhanger in , and had one son, Ferumbras III, born two years later.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, Appendix C, "Took of Great Smials"; J.R.R. Tolkien; Humphrey Carpenter, Christopher Tolkien (eds.), The Letters of J.R.R. Tolkien, Letter 214, (undated, written late 1958 or early 1959)

claims.text: Fortinbras became Thain after his father's death in . It was during his rule when his cousin, Bilbo Baggins, left for his famous adventure.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, Appendix C, "Took of Great Smials"; J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, Appendix B, "The Third Age"

claims.text: He was Thain for 41 years, and after his death in at the age of 102 he was succeeded as Thain by his son Ferumbras; however, in accordance with Took tradition, Lalia continued to be head of the family until her death in .
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien; Humphrey Carpenter, Christopher Tolkien (eds.), The Letters of J.R.R. Tolkien, Letter 214, (undated, written late 1958 or early 1959)
